lines.trans: You must hide in a very reliable place.
Why do I need to hide somewhere right now?
If they begin to interrogate me, I will tell everything.
Therefore even I should not know the address.
And how much time do I need to sit there?
Wait for my call strictly until eight in the evening.
And what if you don't call me on time?
Then immediately give all the important photographs to the police.
Fine, I can go to my friend Lena.
You cannot go to Lena, they will find you there immediately.
Then I will choose another secret place myself.
Well done, be very cautious on the street today.
And right now strict doctors have come to see me.

meanings.note: Street and house number. Common masculine noun meaning 'address' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll give the address: seven Sadovaya Street.

Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.

+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: The neuter form 'всё' used alone. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Neuter всё. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
Plural все. Core Russian det meaning 'all, whole; everyone, everything' in everyday speech.
до вечера = until the evening; вечером = in the evening
E.g. a school evening. Common masculine noun meaning 'evening' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Добрый вечер, Вика. С Новым годом!
examples.trans: Good evening, Vika. Happy New Year!

вовремя.gloss: on time, at the right moment

meanings.en: on time, at the right moment
meanings.note: 'не вовремя' = at a bad moment. Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'время').

examples.text: Ну как же ты не вовремя! Где ты сейчас?
examples.trans: Your timing couldn't be worse! Where are you now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'во-' ('into, up') marks inward or upward movement (stem 'семь').
Used for women too. Common masculine noun meaning 'doctor' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Она там взятки для врачей хранит.
examples.trans: She keeps bribes for the doctors in there.

meanings.note: Проводить время = to spend time. Common neuter noun meaning 'time' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.en: to choose, select; to use up completely (quotas, limits)
meanings.note: + acc. Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'брать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to choose, use up', paired with 'выбирать'.

examples.text: В этом году все квоты выбрали.
examples.trans: This year all the quotas have been used up.
She chose the most beautiful dress.
Agreed, I will choose a movie.

meanings.note: in 'рабочее место' = workplace, job

examples.text: Давай мы его уволим, а тебя на его место назначим.

meanings.note: Agrees with the thing owned. Core Russian det meaning 'my, mine' in everyday speech.

поехать.gloss: to go (by vehicle), to set off

meanings.en: to go, to set off (by car, bus, train)
meanings.note: Мы поедем = We'll be off. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ехать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to go (by vehicle), to set off', paired with 'ехать'.

examples.trans: All right, Arkashenka. We'll be off, it's time.

meanings.note: + dative: 'позвони мне' = call me. Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'звонить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to call, to phone', paired with 'звонить'.

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.note: Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hide (oneself)', paired with 'спрятаться'.

meanings.note: Сам, сама, само, сами. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself (myself, yourself...)' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

meanings.note: Informal. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'идеть'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to sit, to be sitting', paired with 'посидеть'.
